newsitem.title: CANADA: Court rules against CanWest in WIC case.
newsitem.headline: Court rules against CanWest in WIC case.

text.p: The British Columbia Court of Appeal ruled on Thursday against an appeal by CanWest Global Communications Corp in a case involving broadcaster WIC Western International Communications Ltd.
CanWest and two former WIC directors were appealing a decision by a lower court last year that effectively blocked CanWest's C$636 million takeover bid for WIC.
The ruling left in place WIC's two-tier share structure and kept control of the broadcaster in the hands of the Griffiths family of Vancouver, which founded the company.
A ruling in favor of CanWest would have made WIC vulnerable to a takeover bid, analysts said.

CanWest and the former directors sought to have voting rights awarded to WIC's non-voting shareholders. The British Columbia Supreme Court rejected their arguments last year and the case was appealed to the Court of Appeal.

WIC owns some of the most valuable properties in Canadian broadcasting including eight television, 12 radio stations and a share of Canada's CTV network. It has faced mounting shareholder unrest amid complaints the company has performed poorly and is unresponsive to stockholders.

The Griffiths family controls WIC because it owns most of the voting class A shares although it holds only seven percent of WIC's total equity. The two-tier share structure has been a major target of shareholder complaint.
CanWest recently announced it purchased another block of WIC non-voting B shares, bringing its holding to 15 percent. It said it believed itself to be the company's biggest holder of the B shares.
